fundamental_rules.rule: Never directly connect XC7Z045 J58/J59 to a raw 1.8 V net.
fundamental_rules.rationale: 3.3 V drive can violate a 1.8 V input's absolute maximum, and 1.8 V logic-high is not guaranteed at a 3.3 V LVCMOS input.

fundamental_rules.rule: A board connector carrying a protocol name does not determine its electrical standard.
fundamental_rules.rationale: UART has separate 1.8 V raw, 3.3 V TTL and RS-232 stages; CAN has 1.8 V controller logic, 5 V transceiver logic and differential CANH/CANL.

fundamental_rules.rule: Use protocol-specific physical-layer devices for LIN, CAN/CAN FD and RS-232.
fundamental_rules.rationale: A generic CMOS level shifter does not replace the bus transceiver.

board_only_test_strategy.design_constraint: Do not add a universal 1.8 V to 3.3 V adapter board. Reuse on-board 1.8 V resources and only use short signal wires/shunts between existing headers.

interfaces.name: IIC0
coverage: clock stretching where supported by the selected role
conditions: Configure both sides for 1.8 V open-drain operation.
Use the visible STM32-side I2C pull-ups only after confirming fitted resistor population and idle-high level.

interfaces.name: IIC1
interfaces.coverage: Same functional coverage as IIC0; reuse the same STM32 I2C1 firmware because tests are serial.

interfaces.name: LIN1
interfaces.coverage: Same digital-only LIN coverage as LIN0; reuse the same STM32 firmware because tests are serial.

interfaces.name: SPI0..SPI3

stm32_peer.chip_select: Use an exposed U60 GPIO on J35 as software NSS/CS; exact pin is selected in the STM32 board profile.

interfaces.wiring_rule: Connect DUT CLK to STM32 SCK. If DUT is master, DUT MOSI connects to STM32 MISO and DUT MISO connects to STM32 MOSI; reverse the logical roles when STM32 is master. Connect DUT CS to the selected STM32 GPIO.
interfaces.limit: Qualify the maximum clock separately; STM32 peer and flying-wire topology are functional references, not signal-integrity proof.

interfaces.name: QSPI0
interfaces.available_method: Use six STM32 GPIOs on J34/J35 to emulate a very slow QSPI peer or passively sample the transaction.
limitations: STM32F417 has no native Quad-SPI peripheral.
The on-board U26 Quad-SPI flash is connected to separate XC7VX980T configuration nets, not ET6801 QSPI0.
GPIO firmware cannot guarantee flash-slave response timing at normal QSPI clock rates.
interfaces.conclusion: Only basic low-clock protocol and pin-function smoke tests are practical with current board resources; full-rate QSPI remains unsupported.

interfaces.name: EPR_SPI
interfaces.connection: Install J23 shunts 3-4, 5-6, 7-8, 9-10 and 11-12 as required by the test.
interfaces.caution: Preserve or restore EEPROM contents if the test writes data; use a bounded sacrificial address range.

interfaces.name: CANFD
wiring: Ground is already common on the same board; include it in an external cable if connector topology requires.
interfaces.termination: The schematic shows split 60 ohm plus 60 ohm termination networks on CAN4 and CAN5; confirm the resistors are populated before testing.
coverage: classic CAN and CAN FD frames
controller plus level shifter plus transceiver plus CANH/CANL path
limitations: Both protocol controllers are ET6801 instances, so this is not an independent golden implementation.
STM32F417 contains classic CAN 2.0B only and cannot serve as a CAN FD peer.
Malformed-frame and precision fault injection need a separate capable node or dedicated fixture.
